evidence.r1: Glass is limited to navigation, day and venue selection, tickets and the venue menu; programme content is opaque.
evidence.r2: The venue menu opens below the controls without overlapping another glass surface.
evidence.r3: The navigation, two filters, ticket action and temporary menu all serve the programme workflow.
evidence.r4: The navigation, filters and venue menu consistently use pale frosted material.
evidence.r5: No clear-glass treatment is visible; the controls have dense pale frosting over the film still.
evidence.r6: Book tickets is the sole background-tinted action; the selected day uses a neutral dark fill.
evidence.r7: The normal navigation and menu transmit softened image variation, becoming flatter in the reduced-transparency capture.
evidence.r8: Navigation and menu use fixed radii, compact day controls are rounded rectangles, and tickets is a capsule.
evidence.r9: The selected day and inset menu focus outline fit the enclosing rounded surfaces without visibly flared corners.
evidence.r10: Book tickets is a capsule, while the small desktop day and venue controls use rounded rectangles.
evidence.r11: The top bar has four separate glass groups: navigation, day selector, venue selector and tickets.
evidence.r12: Navigation and day actions are text-only; the venue chevron belongs to its text control rather than a separate icon button.
evidence.r13: The material covers the whole navigation and filter controls rather than their inner labels.
evidence.r14: Day and venue groups are deliberately spaced, while each group reads as one continuous material surface.
evidence.r15: The scrolled programme and strands screens show one soft top edge fading content beneath the controls.
evidence.r16: The snowy film still remains behind the controls even when the programme sheet has scrolled into view.
evidence.r17: The opening-film text starts far below the navigation and filter controls.
evidence.r18: Dark labels read clearly on the pale controls, but a dark appearance is not supplied for the required contrast check.
evidence.r19: The reduced-transparency controls remain legible, but increased contrast and reduced motion are not evidenced.
evidence.r20: The opening still fills the entire window, with navigation and ticket controls floating over it.
evidence.r21: The opening text clears the top controls and the lower screens retain an extended film background with a soft boundary.
evidence.r22: A persistent film-image strip and fade sit beneath the controls on the scrolled programme and strands views.
evidence.r23: The open venue-menu still cannot show morphing, materialisation or pointer press feedback.
evidence.r24: Bar labels and menu content are monochrome; the ticket accent is confined to its background.
evidence.r25: Dark control labels stay distinct from the pale snowy imagery behind their frosted surfaces.
